mina: Heads-up — saw a weird increase in host mem growth on a subset of long chat sessions, looks KV related. tagging @sam @raj
sam: can you paste the query/window? which cluster? :mag:
mina: us-west-prod-gpu-pool-3, sampled from 2026-03-10 00:00 to 2026-03-11 00:00. pattern: steady KV residency growth over ~20–30 min sessions then sudden drop spike in evictions.
mina: here's the quick graph: `kv.residency.p50` drifting up, then `kv.evictions.count` spikes aligned with page faults
raj: can you dump the eviction counters? I want to see per-frag vs per-page metrics, and whether the eviction is counted once or per fragment
mina: copied from prom: ```
# HELP kv_evictions_total total eviction events
kv_evictions_total{shard="s3"} 123
kv_evictions_frag_total{shard="s3"} 214
kv_page_faults_total{shard="s3"} 342
# HELP kv_residency_seconds residency distribution
kv_residency_seconds_bucket{le="60"} 1000
kv_residency_seconds_bucket{le="300"} 450
```sam: two oddities: 1) frag counter > eviction counter (suggests one eviction increments frag counter multiple times) 2) page faults high relative to misses
lena: this smells like multi-frag eviction where a single LRU sweep evicts several fragments but we only increment the high-level eviction metric once.
perf-bot: perf-alert: host gw-12 exceeded kv-residency 95th pct for 18m — auto captured heap profile at 2026-03-10T03:14:22Z
sam: can we correlate with kernel selection/batching changes? we rolled out batching heuristic v3 on 2026-03-09
mina: I profiled a host with `pprof top` — top lines show heavy hotspots in `kv_page_eviction_sweep` and `alloc_large_slice`.
mina: snippet:
```
Showing nodes accounting for 62.34s, 78.34% of 79.55s total
  bridge/kv/evict.go:142 (eviction_sweep) 28.12s
  runtime/malloc.go:820 11.34s
  bridge/kv/cache_write.go:87 8.90s
```
raj: if eviction sweep is expensive, that explains CPU+mem blips. But why residency grows slowly? indicates reuse isn't releasing until sweep runs.
lena: hypothesis: our sampling window for residency doesn't attribute reused fragments correctly because we update residency on access but not on cross-slice reuse. also sampler aggregation might be undercounting hits.
sam: propose adding two metrics: `kv_eviction_fragments_evicted_total` and `kv_eviction_ops_total` (ops = logical evictions). That will let us see multi-frag evictions per op.
raj: agreed. also add `kv_reuse_hits_total` (counts when a cached frag is reused within same session) and break down by frag_size_bin.
mina: dashboard ask: per-host heatmap showing frag_evicted_per_op over time, residency p50/p95, reuse_hit_rate, page_fault_rate, and a sparklines row for kernel selection versions.
lena: to debug further, I pushed a small agent build to staging that logs eviction op payloads (sampled 1/1000). can run for 24h and compare.
ops-bot: deploy: staging/kv-evict-trace v0.1 deployed to staging pool at 2026-03-12T14:05:02Z
sam: once we have traces, we can confirm if big sessions produce large contiguous frag clusters that trigger sweeping behavior.
mina: one quick mitigation: lower eviction sweep interval to 30s on a Canary and add a circuit-breaker that avoids sweeping >N frags at once. can test on 5 hosts.
raj: add alert: if frag_evicted_per_op > 8 and reuse_hit_rate < 0.2 for 3m — page-thrash alert.
lena: I'll wire up the dashboard panels in Grafana and create a runbook entry describing: how to interpret frag/op ratio, how to toggle canary sweep interval, and how to pull eviction traces.
mina: thanks — will start the canary in an hour and update. any objections?
sam: no objections. document the perf-bot captures in the runbook.
mina: updating thread with staging logs once available. tl;dr: looks like multi-frag eviction accounting + sweep cost causing mem/CPU spikes and long-tail growth. next: metrics change, dashboard, canary sweep tweak, traces.
